title: introduce-token-provenance-and-explainable-cost-explorer
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: customers and SREs frequently ask why a small subset of requests drives a disproportionate share of token cost and latency. Existing token-level metrics give totals but do not show how tokens map back to request inputs, system stages, and cache/kv behaviors. This PR adds token provenance instrumentation, an explainable cost attribution algorithm, a lightweight provenance sampler, a new Token Provenance Explorer dashboard, and a synthetic request replayer for SLO debugging.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds immutable provenance tags emitted on span creation linking tokens to request inputs, model stages, and cache events. Tags are compact (hex provenance id) and flow through tracing and metric pipelines.
- Introduces a sampling component (provenance-sampler) that captures full token traces for a configurable percent of requests to limit cardinality while preserving coverage across tenants, routes, and model variants.
- Implements an explainable cost allocation operator that attributes per-request token cost to input tokens, prefixes, and intermediate KV-cache contrasts using a time-weighted kernel: cost_share = integral( attention_weight * kv_miss_penalty * time_decay ). The operator runs in rollup worker so it is efficient for high throughput.
- Exposes derived metrics: provenance.token_cost_p50/p90, provenance.kv_miss_share, provenance.prefix_attribution_topk, and provenance.latency_breakdown_by_stage. Metrics include stable labels to avoid cardinality explosion (route, model_family, coarse_input_bucket).
- Adds a Grafana dashboard 'Token Provenance Explorer' and a Redwood Console page to inspect sample traces, cost allocation breakdown, and links to the synthetic replayer.
- Adds a test utility 'provenance-replayer' that can replay a sampled request against a chosen model variant and surface end-to-end token-level timing and cost delta for root-cause analysis.

Why this is safe: provenance tags are optional and default-off; sampling defaults to 0.1% across hosted tenants and can be turned off for private deployments. Cost attribution runs in read-only rollup workers and does not alter serving runtime behavior. The miner keeps label cardinality at bounded levels via coarse bucketing.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema and tag format documented in telemetry/README.md
- [x] Grafana panels added and tested with synthetic traces
- [x] Unit tests for provenance sampler and attribution operator
- [x] Load test showing <2% CPU/regression on rollup workers at 10k rps
- [x] Feature gated behind telemetry.feature_provenance flag

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to the sampling heuristics (observability/provenance/sampler.go) and the rollup aggregation code (observability/rollup/provenance_attrib.go). The attribution math is commented and includes a short worked example. Related Linear tickets ENG-4281 and ENG-4299. Support ticket SUP-8812 requested quick-turn synthetic replayer for a customer incident (included).

review_comments: Ben Liu: high-level LGTM. Two asks: 1) include a note on storage cost for sampled traces, 2) ensure provenance ids are cryptographically non-guessable to avoid info leak.
Aisha Kapoor: addressed both — added TTL-based retention and switched to uuidv7-derived provenance ids in observability/provenance/provenance_tag.go
Marta González: please add a short note in the console about the sample bias and how to interpret sample-level dashboards. Also requested a tooltip explaining the kernel math.
Aisha Kapoor: added dashboard tooltip text and a new section in telemetry/README.md explaining bias and interpretation.
release_notes: Adds optional token provenance tracing, sampling, explainable cost attribution, Token Provenance Explorer dashboard, and a synthetic provenance replayer for SLO debugging. Feature is guarded behind telemetry.feature_provenance.
